To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oestrogens exert neuroprotection against neurodegeneration by modulating the neuronal lipid raft proteome, and that this effect occurs via the activation of signalling platforms that interact with different extracellular signals, as well as via mechanisms aimed at maintaining neuronal membrane integrity.
oestrogens are neuroprotective agents, acting through several mechanisms that include the modulation of signalosomes in lipid rafts.
oestrogen receptor‐mediated neuroprotection against neurodegeneration involves the modulation of neuronal lipid homeostasis and signalosome functionality.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the role of oestrogen receptors and other membrane‐bound proteins in neuronal lipid raft signalosomes and the modulation of neuronal lipid homeostasis by oestrogents as potential mechanisms of action in the prevention of neurodegeneration.

the elucidation of the mechanisms by which oestrogen receptors modulate the function and composition of signalosomes, as well as their role in neuronal membrane homeostasis, in the context of neurodegeneration.
the study of oestrogen mechanisms at the membrane level, which may be of relevance for the development of novel neuroprotective strategies against neurodegeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oestrogenic effects on neurodegeneration may be mediated by several molecular mechanisms, which are not necessarily mutually exclusive.
oestrogens are able to modulate neuronal lipid rafts and signalosomes to exert beneficial actions against different neurodegenerative disorders.
oestrogen receptors are not just a target for oestrogens, but also a tool for oestrogen‐induced modulation of membrane lipid composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oestrogen actions in the brain are not only mediated by its interaction with proteins but also with lipids.
oestrogens act as modulators of neuronal signalosomes and brain lipid homeostasis related to protection against neurodegeneration.
oestrogens act in lipid rafts to maintain the functionality of signalosomes, and also to maintain lipid homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oestrogens, acting through different mechanisms, may be a promising therapeutic tool to preserve neuronal homeostasis and prevent neurodegeneration.
oestrogen actions on neuronal signalosomes and lipid homeostasis may be part of the neuroprotection mechanisms elicited by this hormone.

oestrogens exert their beneficial effects on the brain not only by their interaction with neuronal protein receptors but also through their ability to modulate lipid rafts and lipid homeostasis, and that the interaction between oestrogens, lipid rafts and neuronal lipid homeostasis is a novel area of investigation that may lead to new therapeutic targets against neurodegeneration.
